{"id":"mimid-7yn7.1","title":"Decide: is mimid a full provider or the independent conformance implementation?","description":"Mark, 2026-11-22. The decision that should come BEFORE the hard
blockers are finished, because the two paths diverge sharply after them.

His own framing: '"Plug into all of them" reads as a feature-
completeness problem and isn't.' mimid has interop-tested with ONE
implementation, cooperatively, with its author answering email. The work
is interop testing and it does not compress.

OPTION A: full provider. mimid is a provider people use, federating
with gatekeepers. Needs the whole content list (read receipts, AV
metadata, calls, typing, polls, location, stickers, attachments at
volume), multi-device under load, discovery past a configured peer map,
and a working abuse path across E2EE. This is where mandated interop
VISIBLY fails for users: not refused messages, but messages arriving as
"unsupported content".

OPTION B: the independent conformance implementation. If the EU mandates
MIMI, someone has to be able to CHECK whether the gatekeepers' claims
are true. That is a conformance target, and mimid is already closer to
filling it than any gatekeeper's internal stack: strict decoding, the
fixture-test direction fixed, every ambiguity a decision bead, a
findings log, offline tests. It needs far LESS of the content list,
because a conformance tool has to parse and judge content, not render
it.

What each path makes of the same work:
- The hard blockers are needed either way: catch-up, provider auth,
  ciphersuites, identity. Both paths cross them.
- Content coverage is almost entirely A. A conformance tool needs to
  decode and check content-10, which mimid largely does, not to show a
  sticker.
- Multi-device at volume is mostly A.
- Discovery past the peer map is mostly A. A conformance checker is
  pointed at a target deliberately.
- Franking and reportAbuse are BOTH, and arguably more important to B:
  checking that a gatekeeper's abuse path actually works across E2EE is
  exactly the sort of claim a regulator cannot verify itself.
- The decision-bead discipline and the findings log are B's product.
  Under A they are internal hygiene.

NOT DECIDED. This is Mark's to make, and it is a strategy question, not
a technical one. Recorded so the hard-blocker work is not finished
before it is asked.

Worth noting for either answer: B does not require giving up being a
usable provider, and A does not forbid publishing conformance vectors.
The question is which one sets the priority order when they disagree,
and they disagree about the whole content list.","status":"open","priority":1,"issue_type":"task","owner":"mark@reviewcommit.com","created_at":"2026-11-23T03:51:10.326631754Z","created_by":"Mark Atwood","updated_at":"2026-11-23T03:51:10.326631754Z","labels":["human"],"dependencies":[{"issue_id":"mimid-7yn7.1","depends_on_id":"mimid-7yn7","type":"parent-child","created_at":"2026-11-23T03:51:10.589866117Z","created_by":"Mark Atwood","metadata":"{}"}]}

{"notes":"DEFERRED by Mark, 2026-11-22: revisit after the hard blockers, not now.

His reasoning, and it holds: the hard blockers are needed either way, so
choosing now buys nothing and forecloses a choice that will be better
informed later. The June 2028 document is unknown, and the answer
plausibly depends on what it says.

WHAT MAKES THIS SAFE RATHER THAN A DRIFT INTO NEVER DECIDING: while the
decision is open, spend on the SHARED work and not on the divergent
work. They are cleanly separable:

Shared, do it now, both paths need it:
- follower catch-up (mimid-1wgh.37.104, .1 to .5)
- provider auth at the edges (mimid-7yn7.2) and mTLS with a real peer
  (mimid-6x2f)
- credential types past Basic and did:webvh (mimid-7yn7.4.1)
- ciphersuites and keeping the OpenMLS fork debt down (mimid-7yn7.3,
  mimid-m12g, mimid-1wgh.4.69)
- proving reportAbuse with messages against a second implementation
  (mimid-7yn7.6)
- a second and third implementation to test against (mimid-7yn7.8)

Divergent, do NOT start while this is open:
- the content list (mimid-7yn7.5): read receipts, AV metadata, calls,
  typing, polls, location, stickers. This is the pile the two paths
  disagree about, and it is the expensive one. Starting it is choosing
  the messenger path by default without saying so.
- multi-device at volume (mimid-4lp4) is mostly the messenger path,
  though some of it is needed either way.
- discovery past the configured peer map (mimid-1wgh.37.94) is mostly
  the messenger path: a conformance checker is pointed at a target
  deliberately.

A dependency is wired so mimid-7yn7.5 (content coverage) is blocked by
this bead, which means bd will not offer the divergent work until the
decision is made. That is the mechanism that keeps the deferral honest.

REVISIT WHEN any of these happens, whichever comes first:
1. The hard blockers are done, i.e. catch-up implemented and interop
   tested, provider auth proven with a non-mimid peer, and a credential
   type beyond Basic working both ways.
2. The MIMI drafts reach a final or near-final document, since the
   analysis above is written against -07/-10/-04 and the answer may
   turn on what the RFC actually requires.
3. Anyone external asks mimid to be one or the other: a regulator, a
   gatekeeper, or the WG asking for a reference or conformance
   implementation by name. That would settle it from outside.
4. The January 2027 interop day with Haven (mimid-1wgh.46.20) teaches
   something about how much interop testing really costs, which is the
   number the whole decision turns on.

Item 4 is the near one, and the cheapest source of real information."}
